raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

Let SGLang Simulator obtain optional model-forward costs and independent KV budgets from InferCast while native SGLang retains scheduling, chunk admission and prefix-cache behavior. Source-bound DSPark results can then participate in the existing external closed-loop AgentX coordination protocol.

## Modifications

- Carry immutable prepared-forward work with each result, preserving ordered EXTEND/MIXED work, DECODE histories, sampling, topology, units and explicit unsupported errors. InferCast UMD and the existing resource-budget interfaces remain the model/capacity owners; optional imports stay lazy.
- Bind native DSPark progress and regional costs to exact source/runtime profiles. Validate costs before publishing progress, preserve native output and cancellation accounting, and charge discarded launched tails without exposing their tokens. Acceptance ratios do not become latency multipliers.
- Use the existing UMD operation path for explicit HYBRID costs. Measured exact/supported interpolation takes priority; only a typed numeric miss can use an explicitly selected profile-bound analytic asset. Source bindings are verified independently of numerical coverage, and query ledgers retain measured/theoretical contributions.
- Add explicit TP2/attention-DP2 library transactions: join both actual ordered partitions, keep allocation/CPU vectors/FIFO retirement local, evaluate one joint whole-worker cost/progress result, build both native results before publication, and replicate history only after both publication callbacks succeed. Partial publication failures remain sticky. These entry points leave public ADP2 activation guards closed.
- Project prospective joint work from both prepared reference views and actual independent planner/buffer facts through the existing SDK query contracts. Validate the full materialized capture ladder and role variants before selecting a bucket; completed-frame witnesses are a separate observation path.
- Preserve native overlap, countdown and drained profile semantics in coordinated OFFLINE execution. Consume native result accounting before any post-result terminal/timer Grant, while retaining earlier in-flight timer Grants. Prepare the native controller's spawned callable through the existing early CPU bootstrap.
- Keep native-size packed KV payload storage on meta only in the opt-in CPU bootstrap, preserving logical capacity and real allocator/request ownership. Document source contracts and unsupported configurations.
- Add an internal native attention-DP common-clock bridge. One DPC owns external ingress, paired native budget/dispatch, both result/accounting acknowledgements and a single profile writer; scheduler peers consume the same read-only clock. Preserve waiting/chunked cancellation obligations through both native abort callbacks and paired release acknowledgements.
- Wire typed native selection and worker-forward entry routes through the existing predictor owner, retaining local buffers, capture ladders, counters, first-empty behavior and reset ownership. An explicit joint source binding now validates original startup/capture/proposal/allocated-runtime assets through the existing SDK and constructor. Its narrow TP2/attention-DP2 CPU entry reuses the native DPC, typed worker route and paired clock; all other entry defaults remain unchanged.

## Validation

The earlier broad isolated Linux CPU baseline at `a52183fc810c3f59c7096b78a2f1934c30678f5d` covered all 38 simulator test files: 907 passed / 135 dependency skips without InferCast and 1088 passed / 7 real-data skips with SDK `c902b4904ef0265096e4be61602173ecb619fbbb`. Optional real-data E2E tests were not executed. Later focused counts overlap and are not added to this baseline.

For the current library increments:

- 153 focused peer/reference/runtime/progress CPU controls passed; 74 separate older-SDK ADP1 compatibility controls passed.
- A bounded device-free Linux run executed nine cases using real two-process native GroupCoordinator/Gloo, Req, ScheduleBatch, native result construction and FutureMap publication. Actual loaded module/source identities were verified for both ranks; the container retired with exit 0 and no OOM. Inputs, event setup and duration are explicit protocol fixtures, not measured performance or native Scheduler selection.
- The exact new maintained native controller-entry literal passed in a separate native CPU process. It verifies imports, aliases and forwarding; it does not prove actual Process spawning/unpickling or Engine construction. Private preflight/fixture failures were retained and corrected without modifying native serving source. A previously passed literal was not repeated with the transaction-only successor.
- The result-accounting change passed 91 coordinated CPU/loopback checks. The new assertion reproduced the old source's failure on completed-result Grants while preserving cancellation and earlier timer behavior.
- The joint resolver passed 26 focused CPU checks after the complete-capture-ladder correction. Its cost coordinates matched all six retained completed native frames; missing completion witnesses remained errors. This checks projection semantics, not a causal-progress or latency replay.

For the additional internal-clock and typed-route commits:

- 198 focused CPU controls covered the initial internal clock bridge. A subsequent waiting-request cancellation regression failed on the predecessor and passed with the focused 21-case suite; these overlapping counts are not added together.
- Three bounded device-free Linux controls executed the real native two-process DPC dispatcher/DPBudget, GroupCoordinator/Gloo, Scheduler run loop, Req/ScheduleBatch/FutureMap and result/accounting callbacks at `ce675d8e`. Both ranks reached the same clock/FID, native budgets drained, and the container retired with exit0/no OOM. Loaded source identities were verified. Initial resource/admission/selection, resolver JSON and the 0.01-second whole-worker duration remain explicit fixtures; this does not establish model execution or measured performance.
- The later typed-route increment passed 218 focused CPU controls, including 13 routing cases. Its separate source-assembly check consumed original runtime/profile identities through the real SDK model/resolver contracts without native or GPU imports. It was not executed by the earlier three native clock controls. Older-SDK compatibility checks remain separate.

Additional source-asset and narrow entry validation:

- Original source-asset constructor controls and tamper negatives cover complete runtime identities and the producer allocation filename binding. The default overrides and six existing compatibility owners remain unchanged. The entry increment passes 229 focused CPU controls; these overlap earlier suites and are not added to their totals.
- Three bounded Linux controls at `00a2ca5a` executed the actual source-bound constructor, typed native selection/worker forward and whole-worker UMD HYBRID price with the native DPC/Gloo callbacks. Ragged and either-idle cases finish with one leader cost/progress evaluation, identical paired clocks, accounted callbacks and drained FINISHED. Initial resources/admission/selection remain explicit fixtures; resolved private arguments differ from the new public-entry domain. These controls prove this wiring, not a public Engine/C64 run, measured cost or end-to-end accuracy.

For the explicit source-bound MI355X joint CPU domain, native model-feature validation now uses a function-local target feature view. The original native validator code and its other globals/defaults/closure are retained; runtime/global platform identity, native cache flags and resolved arguments are unchanged. This resolves the bounded-SWA model-feature rejection without disabling the source recipe.166 focused CPU controls pass, including22 actual native-validator positive/negative cases. Independent review covers the narrow activation boundary and unchanged global getter. The later bounded public HTTP/Engine control is described below; complete C64 validation remains pending, and these source controls establish no measured costs or accuracy acceptance.

Repeated DSpark construction now memoizes successful validation of bounded immutable canonical JSON strings (at most32entries/1MiB each), retaining per-instance state and budget checks; mutable parsed objects are not cached. The relevant168 CPU checks pass. Native raw/proxy watchdog activation now preserves its actual owner and supports the native no-op watchdog; all93 checks in its affected CPU file pass. Paired bootstrap administration returns to both native handlers before waiting for first Ready;29 checks pass, including8 new regressions that fail against the exact previous handle. These suites overlap other controls and are not summed. Independent source reviews cover all three scoped commits.

The native public-entry attempt passed readiness and reached the actual Scheduler, but its DP1 reference driver rejected first local-rank binding after the scheduler owner was already established. A scoped fix now seals the first actual rank only on a pristine ledger, independently of that scheduler owner; later rank/ledger changes remain rejected across empty polls and resets. All80 related CPU controls pass,3 native-environment controls are explicitly skipped locally, and the exact old method fails the new hook-order regression. Independent review covered the five-file change. A fresh actual public-entry control completed native Scheduler initialization, server-info, profile start/stop and four original HTTP/SSE requests spanning either-idle and paired partitions. It reached FINISHED with56 output tokens, one profile writer and leader-only cost queries; server, client and container retired with exit0 and no OOM. All18 costs were explicit analytical estimates, so this is bounded functional evidence, not numerical qualification or fullC64 accuracy.

A subsequent full official C64 attempt exposed a finite internal DP exchange waiting across first-Ready preparation. The DPC now returns paired bootstrap polls while no first Ready is readable, retaining the existing ingress pump and all active-run clock, rank, deadline and error guards. The internal30-second deadline is unchanged. A real ZMQ regression fails against the previous source;31 DP and93 adjacent ADP1 controls pass, with independent source review. The later official C64 workflow crossed first Ready and completed its configured virtual profiling window, as scoped below. The historical failure remains separate; bounded logs do not establish a unique historical cause.

Independent source review covered these increments. Full upstream hosted CI remains required before merge.

## Current limits

The native regional path remains source/profile/topology bound. An explicit HYBRID/source-golden joint binding enables the narrow CPU TP2/native-DP1/attention-DP2 path with DP LM head, native local control, built-in TP MoE and unchanged native pool/phase serialization. Constructor source attestation remains mandatory. Bounded public Scheduler/server-info/generation controls and the later official C64 configured workflow have completed. Detailed full-key query evidence remains unavailable for that historical C64 run. No physical-GPU execution or accuracy acceptance is claimed.

Official AgentX 1.0.12 coordinated virtual workflows have completed their configured3600-second profiling windows for ten primary configurations. Nine completed diagnostic exports and one ADP2 diagnostic with detailed query coverage unknown are retained alongside two separate baseline controls. The ADP2 client reports10975 submitted/completed HTTP credits, zero cancelled/errors/in-flight, and a drained router. Its pre-start `full_AgentX_point=false` diagnostic label and grace trigger remain unchanged; neither is itself runtime evidence of missing HTTP requests. DAG future-join/cleanup warnings remain separately recorded, and detailed absent query records cannot be reconstructed from aggregate counters. Historical failed attempts are not spliced into successful results.

These comparisons have substantial coordinate errors and are not an accepted Pareto frontier or hardware-accuracy result. Historical residual-calibrated controls retain their own identities; later cal-none diagnostics and new controlled cost experiments remain separate. A query-route label alone does not identify every numerical contribution.

The optional joint cost-evidence path now creates one exclusive file per actual attention-DP rank (`costs.dp0.jsonl`/`costs.dp1.jsonl`). Both native schedulers construct a predictor, so a single shared exclusive file previously collided before any query. ADP1 and disabled-ledger paths are unchanged; leader-only whole-worker pricing, SDK/UMD writes and numeric/metric formulas are unchanged. The exact six-file increment at `4b55c66bbf7bf05ba9815ca8d77e2b841cd6c88e` passed101 focused CPU tests with zero skips, including real predictor-to-UMD exclusive-writer construction, shared-path failure and repeated-rank rejection. The old source fails the new routing/API regressions. This enables future detailed recording; it does not create a ledger for the historical run or establish new native/accuracy evidence. Full upstream hosted CI remains required before merge.

 ## Serving mode
 
+### Closed-loop workloads
+
+In a closed-loop workload, request completion or a tool timer determines the next
+request. The **workload driver** owns these dependencies, its dataset parser,
+concurrency, warmup, and stopping conditions. The **simulator** owns model request
+scheduling, cache state, and predicted execution time. No dataset schema or agent
+framework is required by the server.
+
+Clients can use either existing execution mode:
+
+| | `BLOCKING`: real time | `OFFLINE` with coordinator: fast-forward |
+|---|---|---|
+| Client | An ordinary HTTP workload driver. | A driver using the coordinator protocol. |
+| Timing | Predicted batch latency is spent sleeping; client timers use real time. | Client and server advance virtual time together. |
+| Metrics | Client measurements include HTTP, tokenization, and scheduling overhead. | The driver uses simulator timestamps. |
+
+Both paths use the same scheduler, cache, and latency predictor. The model output
+is synthetic: the driver must supply response history and workload dependencies
+when replaying a trace. These runs do not evaluate generated answers or agents
+choosing tools from model output. Results depend on the predictor data;
+the bundled replay table is an example, not a hardware performance calibration.
+
+In the explicit CPU simulator, packed DeepSeek KV/index payloads use metadata-only
+storage with their native shape and dtype. Integer allocation, request/window state
+and logical cache capacities remain real CPU state. This allows observed accelerator
+cache capacities without allocating unused model-value tensors on the host; it does
+not change native CUDA execution or estimate the capacity itself.
+
+#### Real-time HTTP clients
+
+Start a small example server from the repository root:
+
+```bash
+export SGLANG_USE_CPU_ENGINE=1
+export CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=""
+export SGLANG_SIMULATOR_OUTPUT_MODE=BLOCKING
+unset SGLANG_SIMULATOR_COORDINATOR
+
+python3 -m sglang_simulator.simulation.sglang.launch_server \
+  --model-path tools/sglang-simulator/test/assets/qwen3-8b \
+  --tokenizer-path tools/sglang-simulator/examples/assets/tokenizer \
+  --chat-template chatml \
+  --sim-config-path tools/sglang-simulator/examples/sim_configs/replay.json \
+  --max-total-tokens 8192 \
+  --disable-overlap-schedule \
+  --skip-server-warmup \
+  --port 30000
+```
+
+Point an HTTP driver at `http://127.0.0.1:30000`. It can use `/generate` or the
+OpenAI-compatible API and issue dependent requests after responses and tool
+waits. No coordinator integration is needed. Requests can run concurrently, but
+a five-second tool wait takes five real seconds. For actual traces, replace the
+example model configuration and tokenizer and set cache capacity for the workload.
+Compare client wall-time metrics separately from simulator logical-time metrics.
+
+#### Fast-forward clients
+
+Restart the server with the same launch command and these environment settings:
+
+```bash
+export SGLANG_SIMULATOR_OUTPUT_MODE=OFFLINE
+export SGLANG_SIMULATOR_COORDINATOR=tcp://127.0.0.1:30001
+```
+
+Run the two-request example:
+
+```bash
+python3 tools/sglang-simulator/examples/closed_loop.py --tool-delay 5
+```
+
+The tool delay advances virtual time without sleeping. For parallel branches
+and a join, restart the server and run
+`python3 tools/sglang-simulator/examples/fork_join.py --tool-delay 5`.
+Both examples use `/generate`; see [the example guide](examples/README.md) to
+adapt the event loop to another dataset. OpenAI HTTP/SSE requests use the same
+protocol by including `rid` in the body. One server handles one run; restarting
+gives the next run a clean clock and cache.
+
+Plain `OFFLINE` cannot account for a client's future requests or tool waits.
+Use `BLOCKING` for clients without coordinator support. Coordination itself
+requires `OFFLINE`.
+
+#### Driver contract
+
+The protocol uses conservative event synchronization: the server advances only
+when the driver has accounted for all work at the current virtual time. The
+transport is JSON over a loopback ZeroMQ REQ/REP connection, separate from HTTP.
+[`AsyncCoordinatorClient`](src/sglang_simulator/simulation/client.py) implements
+the exchange; it does not execute workloads.
+
+The adapter interface is `AsyncCoordinatorClient` and the `Ready`, `Submit`,
+`Cancel`, `Grant`, and `Terminal` message types in
+[`simulation.coordinator`](src/sglang_simulator/simulation/coordinator.py).
+The server-side `Coordinator`, scheduler bridge, and native request objects are
+implementation details; workload adapters should not depend on them.
+
+Protocol version 1 has two messages:
+
+| Message | Fields |
+|---|---|
+| `Ready` | Stable `run_id`, sequential `round` starting at 0, ordered `operations` (`{"type":"submit","rid":"..."}` or `{"type":"cancel","rid":"..."}`), optional `next_wakeup_ns`, and `finished`. A cancel may include `reason`. |
+| `Grant` | Matching `run_id` and `round`, `now_ns`, `terminals` (`rid`, `kind`, `at_ns`, optional `reason`), and `status` (`CONTINUE`, `FINISHED`, or `ERROR` with `error`). Terminal kinds are `COMPLETED`, `CANCELLED`, and `ERROR`. |
+
+Both carry `protocol_version: 1`; only one `Ready` may be outstanding. All times
+are integer nanoseconds relative to the run. The earliest pending client timer
+is `next_wakeup_ns`; omit it when no timer is pending. Each round follows these rules:
+
+1. Process current completions and timers, including work their callbacks create.
+   Start HTTP requests concurrently with `Ready`; its submits form the input
+   barrier, so the server waits for every active submitted payload before advancing.
+2. Read `Grant` and consume HTTP results for its completed requests before
+   releasing dependent work. A timer-only grant needs no HTTP result; other
+   requests may remain pending across rounds. Do not wait for all pending HTTP
+   requests before sending the next `Ready`, or release dependencies on HTTP
+   arrival alone.
+3. When stopping, submit required cancels and set `finished`. Continue consuming
+   terminals and sending finished rounds until `FINISHED` confirms native cleanup.
+
+Use unique, equal-length request IDs within a run: SGLang's native cancellation
+matches ID prefixes. The HTTP pool must admit every request in a round without
+waiting for earlier responses; the examples use a dedicated unlimited aiohttp
+pool and control workload concurrency explicitly. Protocol watchdogs use real
+time to detect failures. They do not advance simulated time, and a timed-out
+exchange must not be retried on the same run.
+
+The initial scope is one local driver and scheduler, text generation with
+ordinary radix cache, and completion-triggered workflows. HiCache, PD, explicit
+sessions, LoRA, and asynchronous grammar are rejected. Speculation is limited to
+the explicit source-bound native DSPark profile: its original overlap loop,
+FutureMap and reference ledger retain native event order. Every result advances
+virtual time by its own forward duration, and already launched native tails drain
+before FINISHED even after all requests become terminal. Discarded tails add no
+visible output-token event.
+Native profile start/stop administration is allowed before the first driver Ready
+and after FINISHED with all native results drained. It is rejected during an
+active coordinated run so resetting accounting cannot discard pending work.
+Coordinated runs preserve native `--prefill-decode-interval` countdowns when the
+runtime exposes the validated cadence helper and schedule-pass surfaces. A
+cadence-only pass with pending native work consumes no modeled forward time:
+it neither advances the clock nor grants a future client timer. Unsupported
+native cadence surfaces fail before coordinator binding. Other compatibility
+guards, including other speculative algorithms and DP attention, remain unchanged.
+
+Phase deadlines are driver-owned virtual timers; native wall-time waiting/running
+timeouts must be disabled. HTTP/SSE transport and predictor execution time do not
+contribute to virtual CPU overhead. Unmodeled frontend/CPU costs are zero.
+Predicted batch durations must be positive at nanosecond resolution; a zero-cost
+fallback is rejected rather than allowing an endless workload at one timestamp.
+
+Startup generation warmup is skipped. The driver may perform workload/cache
+warmup, then start its measurement window without resetting cache state. Warmup
+requests and time must be excluded from benchmark results.
+Administrative resets and profiling requests are rejected. Harness-specific
+phase scheduling and metric aggregation remain in that harness's adapter.
+
+#### Output and metrics
+
+For fixed-length trace replay, request the desired output length with
+`ignore_eos: true`. Prompt lengths depend on the supplied tokenizer and chat
+template; use actual server token and cache counts for metrics. Trace-declared
+lengths and synthetic output text do not establish cache reuse by themselves.
+
+Coordinated `/generate` responses include a timing snapshot under
+`meta_info.sglang_simulator`. Streaming chat (`/v1/chat/completions`, `n=1`)
+emits the same snapshot as an additional SSE event before each native content output:
+
+```text
+event: sglang_simulator
+data: {"version":1,"rid":"request0","arrival_ns":0,"first_token_ns":10000000,"last_token_ns":30000000,"commit_ns":30000000,"terminal_ns":30000000,"prompt_tokens":7,"completion_tokens":3,"cached_tokens":0}
+```
+
+All times are integer nanoseconds relative to the coordinated run. Arrival is
+the `Submit` time; first/last token times are native visible-token commits after
+the modeled batch finishes. `commit_ns` is the current result's commit time.
+`terminal_ns` is null until native completion; first/last are null until a token
+is committed. A result with no new tokens leaves first/last unchanged. Counts
+come from native prompt, visible output and cache state; cache reporting is
+enabled automatically for coordinated runs.
+
+Snapshots use constant space per request and preserve first/last times when
+streaming chunks are coalesced or emitted less frequently. They do not contain
+per-token timestamps, so they support TTFT, completion latency and mean TPOT,
+not per-token ITL percentiles. The initial empty role chunk can precede the first
+snapshot. For streaming chat metrics, request `stream_options: {"include_usage": true}`
+and validate the terminal snapshot against final usage before consuming `[DONE]`.
+Non-streaming `/generate` returns its snapshot and counts in the JSON response.
+Cancellation before a token commit retains the native abort response.
+
+The ordinary HTTP path is covered by `test_simulation_blocking_agentic.py`;
+`test_simulation_blocking_pacing.py` checks cache-load response timing.
+Focused coordinator tests are `test_simulation_coordinator.py`,

+`test_simulation_coordinated_serving.py`. Run test files in separate processes,
+as simulator hooks cache configuration at import time.

+"""Two dependent HTTP requests separated by a virtual tool delay."""
+
+import argparse
+import asyncio
+import json
+import uuid
+
+import aiohttp
+from sglang_simulator.simulation.client import AsyncCoordinatorClient
+from sglang_simulator.simulation.coordinator import Ready, Submit
+
+
+async def run(base_url: str, coordinator: str, tool_delay_s: float) -> list[dict]:
+    run_id = uuid.uuid4().hex
+    connector = aiohttp.TCPConnector(limit=0, limit_per_host=0)
+    async with (
+        aiohttp.ClientSession(
+            connector=connector, timeout=aiohttp.ClientTimeout(total=30)
+        ) as http,
+        AsyncCoordinatorClient(coordinator) as control,
+    ):
+        round_id = 0
+        events = []
+        for turn in range(2):
+            rid = f"{run_id}.{turn:016x}"
+
+            async def send(rid=rid, turn=turn):
+                async with http.post(
+                    f"{base_url}/generate",
+                    json={
+                        "rid": rid,
+                        "input_ids": [17] * (32 + turn),
+                        "sampling_params": {
+                            "max_new_tokens": 4,
+                            "ignore_eos": True,
+                        },
+                    },
+                ) as response:
+                    response.raise_for_status()
+                    return await response.json()
+
+            tasks = (
+                asyncio.create_task(send()),
+                asyncio.create_task(
+                    control.request(Ready(run_id, round_id, [Submit(rid)]))
+                ),
+            )
+            try:
+                _, grant = await asyncio.gather(*tasks)
+            finally:
+                # A failed exchange aborts the run; reap its HTTP/control peer.
+                for task in tasks:
+                    task.cancel()
+                await asyncio.gather(*tasks, return_exceptions=True)
+            if len(grant.terminals) != 1 or grant.terminals[0].kind != "COMPLETED":
+                raise RuntimeError(f"unexpected request terminal: {grant}")
+            events.append({"turn": turn, "completed_ns": grant.now_ns})
+            round_id += 1
+            if turn == 0:
+                await control.request(
+                    Ready(
+                        run_id,
+                        round_id,
+                        [],
+                        next_wakeup_ns=grant.now_ns + round(tool_delay_s * 1e9),
+                    )
+                )
+                round_id += 1
+        await control.request(Ready(run_id, round_id, [], finished=True))
+        return events
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
+    parser.add_argument("--base-url", default="http://127.0.0.1:30000")
+    parser.add_argument("--coordinator", default="tcp://127.0.0.1:30001")
+    parser.add_argument("--tool-delay", type=float, default=5.0)
+    args = parser.parse_args()
+    if not 0 <= args.tool_delay < float("inf"):
+        parser.error("--tool-delay must be nonnegative and finite")
+    print(
+        json.dumps(
+            asyncio.run(run(args.base_url, args.coordinator, args.tool_delay)), indent=2
+        )
+    )

+"""A reference driver: root -> tool wait -> two parallel requests -> join."""
+
+import argparse
+import asyncio
+import json
+import math
+import uuid
+
+import aiohttp
+from sglang_simulator.simulation.client import AsyncCoordinatorClient
+from sglang_simulator.simulation.coordinator import Ready, Submit
+
+
+async def generate(http, base_url, payload):
+    async with http.post(f"{base_url}/generate", json=payload) as response:
+        response.raise_for_status()
+        return await response.json()
+
+
+async def run(base_url, coordinator, tool_delay_s=5.0, *, send=generate):
+    if not math.isfinite(tool_delay_s) or tool_delay_s < 0:
+        raise ValueError("tool_delay_s must be nonnegative and finite")
+    run_id = uuid.uuid4().hex
+    tasks, names, arrivals, results = {}, {}, {}, {}
+    operations, events = [], []
+    now_ns = round_id = 0
+    wakeup_ns = None
+    prompt = [17] * 8
+    # HTTP can fail before the scheduler sees its payload and grants any event.
+    failure = asyncio.get_running_loop().create_future()
+
+    def check_http(task):
+        if not task.cancelled() and (error := task.exception()) is not None:
+            if not failure.done():
+                failure.set_result(error)
+
+    async def checked(awaitable):
+        task = asyncio.ensure_future(awaitable)
+        try:
+            await asyncio.wait((task, failure), return_when=asyncio.FIRST_COMPLETED)
+            if failure.done():
+                raise failure.result()
+            return await task
+        finally:
+            if not task.done():
+                task.cancel()
+            await asyncio.gather(task, return_exceptions=True)
+
+    # Transport capacity must not prevent a round's payloads from arriving.
+    connector = aiohttp.TCPConnector(limit=0, limit_per_host=0)
+    async with (
+        aiohttp.ClientSession(
+            connector=connector, timeout=aiohttp.ClientTimeout(total=30)
+        ) as http,
+        AsyncCoordinatorClient(coordinator) as control,
+    ):
+
+        def submit(name, input_ids, output_length):
+            rid = f"{run_id}.{len(names):016x}"
+            names[rid] = name
+            arrivals[name] = now_ns
+            tasks[rid] = asyncio.create_task(
+                send(
+                    http,
+                    base_url,
+                    {
+                        "rid": rid,
+                        "input_ids": input_ids,
+                        "sampling_params": {
+                            "max_new_tokens": output_length,
+                            "ignore_eos": True,
+                        },
+                    },
+                )
+            )
+            tasks[rid].add_done_callback(check_http)
+            operations.append(Submit(rid))
+
+        try:
+            submit("root", prompt, 2)
+            while True:
+                grant = await checked(
+                    control.request(
+                        Ready(
+                            run_id,
+                            round_id,
+                            operations,
+                            next_wakeup_ns=wakeup_ns,
+                            finished=len(results) == 4,
+                        )
+                    )
+                )
+                operations = []
+                round_id += 1
+                now_ns = grant.now_ns
+                for terminal in grant.terminals:
+                    if terminal.kind != "COMPLETED":
+                        raise RuntimeError(f"request failed: {terminal}")
+                    # Do not await other branches: they may need another Ready.
+                    body = await checked(tasks[terminal.rid])
+                    del tasks[terminal.rid]
+                    name = names[terminal.rid]
+                    results[name] = body["output_ids"]
+                    events.append(
+                        {
+                            "node": name,
+                            "arrival_ns": arrivals[name],
+                            "completed_ns": terminal.at_ns,
+                            "output_tokens": body["meta_info"]["completion_tokens"],
+                        }
+                    )
+                    if name == "root":
+                        wakeup_ns = now_ns + round(tool_delay_s * 1e9)
+
+                # Apply all workload transitions before yielding the clock.
+                if wakeup_ns is not None and now_ns >= wakeup_ns:
+                    wakeup_ns = None
+                    prefix = prompt + results["root"]
+                    submit("left", prefix + [19] * 8, 2)
+                    submit("right", prefix + [23] * 8, 6)
+                if "left" in results and "right" in results and len(names) == 3:
+                    submit("join", prompt + results["left"] + results["right"], 1)
+                if grant.status == "FINISHED":
+                    return events
+        finally:
+            # Failure aborts this run; closing HTTP alone is not a simulated Cancel.
+            for task in tasks.values():
+                task.cancel()
+            await asyncio.gather(*tasks.values(), return_exceptions=True)
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
+    parser.add_argument("--base-url", default="http://127.0.0.1:30000")
+    parser.add_argument("--coordinator", default="tcp://127.0.0.1:30001")
+    parser.add_argument("--tool-delay", type=float, default=5.0)
+    args = parser.parse_args()
+    if not math.isfinite(args.tool_delay) or args.tool_delay < 0:
+        parser.error("--tool-delay must be nonnegative and finite")
+    print(
+        json.dumps(
+            asyncio.run(run(args.base_url, args.coordinator, args.tool_delay)), indent=2
+        )
+    )

+"""Async control client; model payloads still use the existing HTTP API."""
+
+import asyncio
+import math
+
+import zmq
+import zmq.asyncio
+from sglang_simulator.compat import validate_coordinator_endpoint
+from sglang_simulator.simulation.coordinator import (
+    PROTOCOL_VERSION,
+    Grant,
+    ProtocolError,
+    Ready,
+    decode_grant,
+    encode_message,
+)
+
+
+class AsyncCoordinatorClient:
+    """One outstanding exchange, with wall-clock failure detection.
+
+    A timeout makes the client unusable: retrying an ambiguous exchange could
+    acknowledge results that the workload never consumed.
+    """
+
+    def __init__(self, endpoint: str, *, timeout_s: float = 30.0):
+        self.endpoint = validate_coordinator_endpoint(endpoint)
+        if not math.isfinite(timeout_s) or timeout_s <= 0:
+            raise ValueError("timeout_s must be positive and finite")
+        self.timeout_s = timeout_s
+        self._context = zmq.asyncio.Context()
+        self._socket = self._context.socket(zmq.REQ)
+        self._socket.setsockopt(zmq.LINGER, 0)
+        self._socket.setsockopt(zmq.IPV6, 1)
+        self._socket.connect(self.endpoint)
+        self._inflight = False
+        self._closed = False
+        self._now_ns = 0
+
+    async def request(self, ready: Ready) -> Grant:
+        if self._closed:
+            raise ProtocolError("coordinator client is closed")
+        if self._inflight:
+            raise ProtocolError("only one Ready may be outstanding")
+        self._inflight = True
+        try:
+            grant = await asyncio.wait_for(self._exchange(ready), self.timeout_s)
+            if (
+                grant.protocol_version != PROTOCOL_VERSION
+                or grant.run_id != ready.run_id
+                or grant.round != ready.round
+                or grant.now_ns < self._now_ns
+            ):
+                raise ProtocolError("Grant does not match the outstanding Ready")
+            if grant.status == "ERROR":
+                raise ProtocolError(grant.error or "coordinator reported a run failure")
+            self._now_ns = grant.now_ns
+            if grant.status == "FINISHED":
+                self.close()
+            return grant
+        except asyncio.TimeoutError as exc:
+            self.close()
+            raise ProtocolError(
+                f"run={ready.run_id!r} round={ready.round}: "
+                f"coordinator did not reply within {self.timeout_s} wall seconds"
+            ) from exc
+        except BaseException:
+            self.close()
+            raise
+        finally:
+            self._inflight = False
+
+    async def _exchange(self, ready: Ready) -> Grant:
+        await self._socket.send(encode_message(ready))
+        return decode_grant(await self._socket.recv())
+
+    def close(self) -> None:
+        if not self._closed:
+            self._closed = True
+            self._socket.close(linger=0)
+            self._context.term()
+
+    async def __aenter__(self) -> "AsyncCoordinatorClient":  # noqa: PYI034
+        return self
+
+    async def __aexit__(self, exc_type, exc_value, traceback) -> None:
+        self.close()

+"""Transport-independent state for an OFFLINE simulator's external driver.
+
+The scheduler owns payloads and batch execution. This module only records the
+driver's causal promise, checks the input barrier, and commits virtual events.
+"""
+
+from collections import deque
+from typing import Literal
+
+import msgspec
+
+PROTOCOL_VERSION = 1
+
+
+class ProtocolError(ValueError):
+    """The run cannot continue without violating the coordination contract."""
+
+
+class Submit(msgspec.Struct, tag="submit", forbid_unknown_fields=True, frozen=True):
+    rid: str
+
+
+class Cancel(msgspec.Struct, tag="cancel", forbid_unknown_fields=True, frozen=True):
+    rid: str
+    reason: str = "cancelled by driver"
+
+
+Operation = Submit | Cancel
+TerminalKind = Literal["COMPLETED", "CANCELLED", "ERROR"]
+
+
+class Ready(msgspec.Struct, forbid_unknown_fields=True, frozen=True):
+    run_id: str
+    round: int
+    operations: list[Operation]
+    next_wakeup_ns: int | None = None
+    finished: bool = False
+    protocol_version: int = PROTOCOL_VERSION
+
+
+class Terminal(msgspec.Struct, forbid_unknown_fields=True, frozen=True):
+    rid: str
+    kind: TerminalKind
+    at_ns: int
+    reason: str | None = None
+
+
+class Grant(msgspec.Struct, forbid_unknown_fields=True, frozen=True):
+    run_id: str
+    round: int
+    now_ns: int
+    terminals: list[Terminal]
+    status: Literal["CONTINUE", "FINISHED", "ERROR"] = "CONTINUE"
+    error: str | None = None
+    protocol_version: int = PROTOCOL_VERSION
+
+
+_ENCODER = msgspec.json.Encoder()
+_READY_DECODER = msgspec.json.Decoder(Ready)
+_GRANT_DECODER = msgspec.json.Decoder(Grant)
+
+
+def encode_message(message: Ready | Grant) -> bytes:
+    return _ENCODER.encode(message)
+
+
+def decode_ready(data: bytes) -> Ready:
+    try:
+        return _READY_DECODER.decode(data)
+    except msgspec.DecodeError as exc:
+        raise ProtocolError(f"Invalid Ready: {exc}") from exc
+
+
+def decode_grant(data: bytes) -> Grant:
+    try:
+        return _GRANT_DECODER.decode(data)
+    except msgspec.DecodeError as exc:
+        raise ProtocolError(f"Invalid Grant: {exc}") from exc
+
+
+class _Request(msgspec.Struct):
+    sequence: int
+    arrival_ns: int
+    admitted: bool = False
+    terminal: Terminal | None = None
+
+
+class Coordinator:
+    """One driver, one outstanding Ready, and one authoritative virtual clock."""
+
+    def __init__(self, run_id: str | None = None):
+        self.run_id = run_id
+        self.now_ns = 0
+        self.next_round = 0
+        self._ready: Ready | None = None
+        self._requests: dict[str, _Request] = {}
+        self._pending: deque[str] = deque()
+        self._terminals: list[Terminal] = []
+        self._driver_finished = False
+        self._closed = False
+
+    @property
+    def awaiting_ready(self) -> bool:
+        return self._ready is None and not self._closed
+
+    @property
+    def next_wakeup_ns(self) -> int | None:
+        return self._ready.next_wakeup_ns if self._ready is not None else None
+
+    @property
+    def driver_finished(self) -> bool:
+        return self._driver_finished
+
+    @property
+    def has_terminals(self) -> bool:
+        return bool(self._terminals)
+
+    @property
+    def pending_rids(self) -> tuple[str, ...]:
+        """Payloads required by this Ready, in manifest order."""
+        self._skip_terminal_payloads()
+        return tuple(rid for rid in self._pending if self.is_open(rid))
+
+    def _skip_terminal_payloads(self) -> None:
+        # Cancelled or rejected payloads can be skipped without an HTTP arrival.
+        # Each entry leaves this queue once, including cancellations out of order.
+        while self._pending and not self.is_open(self._pending[0]):
+            self._pending.popleft()
+
+    @property
+    def open_rids(self) -> tuple[str, ...]:
+        return tuple(rid for rid in self._requests if self.is_open(rid))
+
+    def is_open(self, rid: str) -> bool:
+        request = self._requests.get(rid)
+        return request is not None and request.terminal is None
+
+    def request_arrival_ns(self, rid: str) -> int:
+        """Return the manifest arrival without a float clock conversion."""
+        try:
+            return self._requests[rid].arrival_ns
+        except KeyError as exc:
+            raise self._error(f"unknown request rid={rid!r}") from exc
+
+    def is_terminal(self, rid: str) -> bool:
+        request = self._requests.get(rid)
+        return request is not None and request.terminal is not None
+
+    def is_cancelled(self, rid: str) -> bool:
+        request = self._requests.get(rid)
+        return (
+            request is not None
+            and request.terminal is not None
+            and request.terminal.kind == "CANCELLED"
+        )
+
+    def _error(self, message: str) -> ProtocolError:
+        return ProtocolError(
+            f"run={self.run_id!r} round={self.next_round} now_ns={self.now_ns}: "
+            f"{message}"
+        )
+
+    def accept_ready(self, ready: Ready) -> None:
+        """Validate the whole manifest before modifying any run state."""
+        if self._closed:
+            raise self._error("run already finished")
+        if self._ready is not None:
+            raise self._error("previous Ready has not received its Grant")
+        if ready.protocol_version != PROTOCOL_VERSION:
+            raise self._error(f"unsupported protocol version {ready.protocol_version}")
+        if not ready.run_id or len(ready.run_id) > 128:
+            raise self._error("run_id must contain 1 to 128 characters")
+        if self.run_id is not None and ready.run_id != self.run_id:
+            raise self._error(f"unexpected run_id {ready.run_id!r}")
+        if type(ready.round) is not int or ready.round != self.next_round:
+            raise self._error(f"expected round {self.next_round}, got {ready.round!r}")
+        wakeup = ready.next_wakeup_ns
+        if wakeup is not None and (type(wakeup) is not int or wakeup < self.now_ns):
+            raise self._error(f"next_wakeup_ns precedes now: {wakeup!r}")
+        if self._driver_finished and not ready.finished:
+            raise self._error("finished driver cannot resume work")
+        if ready.finished and wakeup is not None:
+            raise self._error("finished driver cannot register a timer")
+
+        submitted: set[str] = set()
+        for op in ready.operations:
+            if not isinstance(op, (Submit, Cancel)):
+                raise self._error(f"unsupported operation {type(op).__name__}")
+            if not op.rid or len(op.rid) > 256:
+                raise self._error("rid must contain 1 to 256 characters")
+            if isinstance(op, Submit):
+                if ready.finished:
+                    raise self._error(f"finished driver submitted rid={op.rid!r}")
+                if op.rid in self._requests or op.rid in submitted:
+                    raise self._error(f"duplicate Submit rid={op.rid!r}")
+                submitted.add(op.rid)
+            elif op.rid not in self._requests and op.rid not in submitted:
+                raise self._error(f"Cancel for unknown rid={op.rid!r}")
+
+        self.run_id = ready.run_id
+        self._ready = ready
+        self._driver_finished = ready.finished
+        for op in ready.operations:
+            if isinstance(op, Submit):
+                self._requests[op.rid] = _Request(len(self._requests), self.now_ns)
+                self._pending.append(op.rid)
+            else:
+                self.terminal(op.rid, "CANCELLED", reason=op.reason)
+
+    def mark_admitted(self, rid: str) -> None:
+        if self._ready is None:
+            raise self._error(f"cannot admit rid={rid!r} before Ready")
+        self._skip_terminal_payloads()
+        if not self._pending or rid != self._pending[0]:
+            raise self._error(
+                f"payload rid={rid!r} is not next in manifest {self.pending_rids}"
+            )
+        self._pending.popleft()
+        self._requests[rid].admitted = True
+
+    def advance(self, now_ns: int) -> None:
+        if self._ready is None:
+            raise self._error("cannot advance before Ready")
+        if type(now_ns) is not int or now_ns < self.now_ns:
+            raise self._error(f"virtual time cannot go backwards: {now_ns!r}")
+        if self.pending_rids:
+            raise self._error(f"missing payloads for {self.pending_rids}")
+        if self.has_terminals and now_ns > self.now_ns:
+            raise self._error("must deliver terminal events before advancing")
+        if self.next_wakeup_ns is not None and now_ns > self.next_wakeup_ns:
+            raise self._error(f"cannot advance past timer at {self.next_wakeup_ns}")
+        self.now_ns = now_ns
+
+    def terminal(
+        self, rid: str, kind: TerminalKind, *, reason: str | None = None
+    ) -> bool:
+        """Commit at most one terminal; late native completions are ignored."""
+        request = self._requests.get(rid)
+        if request is None:
+            raise self._error(f"terminal for unknown rid={rid!r}")
+        if kind not in ("COMPLETED", "CANCELLED", "ERROR"):
+            raise self._error(f"invalid terminal kind {kind!r}")
+        if request.terminal is not None:
+            return False
+        if self._ready is None:
+            raise self._error(f"cannot commit rid={rid!r} before Ready")
+        if kind == "COMPLETED" and not request.admitted:
+            raise self._error(f"cannot complete unadmitted rid={rid!r}")
+        event = Terminal(rid, kind, self.now_ns, reason)
+        request.terminal = event
+        self._terminals.append(event)
+        return True
+
+    def grant(self, *, finished: bool = False) -> Grant:
+        """Close this round after the bridge has applied all scheduler work.
+
+        The bridge must additionally check batch and native cleanup state before
+        requesting FINISHED; a cancelled request can still occupy a batch.
+        """
+        if self._ready is None:
+            raise self._error("no Ready to answer")
+        if self.pending_rids:
+            raise self._error(f"missing payloads for {self.pending_rids}")
+        if finished and (not self.driver_finished or self.open_rids):
+            raise self._error("cannot finish with an active driver or open requests")
+        terminals = sorted(
+            self._terminals, key=lambda event: self._requests[event.rid].sequence
+        )
+        result = Grant(
+            self.run_id,
+            self.next_round,
+            self.now_ns,
+            terminals,
+            "FINISHED" if finished else "CONTINUE",
+        )
+        self.next_round += 1
+        self._ready = None
+        self._terminals = []
+        self._closed = finished
+        return result

+"""Optional InferCast resource budgets for the declared target deployment."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import hashlib
+import json
+import math
+import re
+from collections.abc import Mapping
+from pathlib import Path
+from typing import TYPE_CHECKING
+
+if TYPE_CHECKING:
+    from sglang_simulator.simulation.types import SchedulerConfig
+    from sglang_simulator.spec.accelerator import AcceleratorInfo
+    from sglang_simulator.spec.model import ModelInfo
+
+_FULL_COMMIT = re.compile(r"^[0-9a-f]{40}$")
+_CONFIG_FIELDS = {
+    "provider",
+    "provider_revision",
+    "model_id",
+    "model_revision",
+    "policy",
+    "shared_expert_tp_size",
+}
+_STRUCTURAL_FIELDS = {
+    "architectures",
+    "hidden_size",
+    "num_hidden_layers",
+    "num_attention_heads",
+    "num_key_value_heads",
+    "head_dim",
+    "attention_head_dim",
+    "v_head_dim",
+    "intermediate_size",
+    "vocab_size",
+    "tie_word_embeddings",
+    "attention_bias",
+    "mlp_bias",
+    "qk_nope_head_dim",
+    "qk_rope_head_dim",
+    "kv_lora_rank",
+    "q_lora_rank",
+    "moe_intermediate_size",
+    "n_routed_experts",
+    "n_shared_experts",
+    "first_k_dense_replace",
+    "moe_layer_freq",
+    "moe_router_dtype",
+    "router_fp32",
+    "topk_method",
+    "quantization_config",
+}
+
+
+def _dtype_name(value) -> str:
+    name = str(getattr(value, "value", value)).removeprefix("torch.").lower()
+    return {"bf16": "bfloat16", "fp16": "float16", "fp32": "float32"}.get(name, name)
+
+
+def _validate_loaded_model(
+    model: ModelInfo, resources, config_path: Path, target_config: SchedulerConfig
+) -> None:
+    payload = config_path.read_bytes()
+    if hashlib.sha256(payload).hexdigest() != resources.provenance.config_sha256:
+        raise ValueError(
+            "local config.json changed during InferCast resource estimation"
+        )
+    source = json.loads(payload)
+    effective = model.hf_config
+    if callable(getattr(effective, "to_dict", None)):
+        effective = effective.to_dict()
+    if not isinstance(effective, Mapping):
+        raise ValueError("memory_budget requires materialized model hf_config")  # noqa: TRY004
+    mismatches = {
+        name: {"loaded": effective.get(name), "source": source[name]}
+        for name in _STRUCTURAL_FIELDS & source.keys()
+        if effective.get(name) != source[name]
+    }
+    if effective.get("quantization_config") != source.get("quantization_config"):
+        mismatches["quantization_config"] = {
+            "loaded": effective.get("quantization_config"),
+            "source": source.get("quantization_config"),
+        }
+    for name in (
+        "hidden_size",
+        "num_hidden_layers",
+        "num_attention_heads",
+        "num_key_value_heads",
+        "head_dim",
+        "v_head_dim",
+        "vocab_size",
+        "kv_lora_rank",
+        "qk_rope_head_dim",
+        "qk_nope_head_dim",
+    ):
+        value = getattr(model, name)
+        if name in source and value is not None and value != source[name]:
+            mismatches[name] = {"loaded": value, "source": source[name]}
+    if mismatches:
+        raise ValueError(
+            f"loaded model resource geometry differs from config.json: {mismatches}"
+        )
+    expected_arch = {"LLAMA": "MHA", "DEEPSEEK": "MLA"}.get(resources.family)
+    if expected_arch is not None and model.attention_arch != expected_arch:
+        raise ValueError(
+            "loaded attention layout differs from InferCast resource layout"
+        )
+    embedding = next(
+        tensor for tensor in resources.tensors if tensor.role == "embedding"
+    )
+    if _dtype_name(model.torch_dtype) != embedding.storage.data_dtype:
+        raise ValueError(
+            "loaded model torch_dtype differs from InferCast resource storage"
+        )
+    if (
+        target_config.data_type is not None
+        and _dtype_name(target_config.data_type) != embedding.storage.data_dtype
+    ):
+        raise ValueError("target data_type differs from InferCast resource storage")
+
+
+def estimate_infercast_budget(
+    model: ModelInfo,
+    hw: AcceleratorInfo,
+    target_config: SchedulerConfig,
+    budget_config: Mapping,
+) -> tuple[int, dict]:
+    """Return logical token capacity and a compact, attributable budget summary."""
+    if not isinstance(budget_config, Mapping):
+        raise ValueError("memory_budget must be an object")  # noqa: TRY004
+    unknown = set(budget_config) - _CONFIG_FIELDS
+    if unknown:
+        raise ValueError(f"unknown memory_budget fields: {sorted(unknown)}")
+    if budget_config.get("provider") != "infercast":
+        raise ValueError("memory_budget.provider must be 'infercast'")
+    model_id = budget_config.get("model_id")
+    if not isinstance(model_id, str) or not model_id or model_id != model_id.strip():
+        raise ValueError("memory_budget.model_id must be a nonempty trimmed string")
+    revision = budget_config.get("provider_revision")
+    if not isinstance(revision, str) or not _FULL_COMMIT.fullmatch(revision):
+        raise ValueError(
+            "memory_budget.provider_revision must be a full lowercase commit"
+        )
+    model_revision = budget_config.get("model_revision")
+    if model_revision is not None and (
+        not isinstance(model_revision, str)
+        or not _FULL_COMMIT.fullmatch(model_revision)
+    ):
+        raise ValueError(
+            "memory_budget.model_revision must be null or a full lowercase commit"
+        )
+    if not isinstance(budget_config.get("policy"), Mapping):
+        raise ValueError("memory_budget.policy must be an explicit object")  # noqa: TRY004
+    if type(target_config.dp_size) is not int or target_config.dp_size != 1:
+        raise ValueError("InferCast memory budgets require target dp_size=1")
+    if type(target_config.cp_size) is not int or target_config.cp_size != 1:
+        raise ValueError("InferCast memory budgets require target cp_size=1")
+    if (
+        not isinstance(model.model_path, (str, Path))
+        or not str(model.model_path).strip()
+    ):
+        raise ValueError(
+            "InferCast memory budgets require a local model config directory"
+        )
+    kv_dtype = getattr(target_config.kv_cache_data_type, "value", None)
+    if not isinstance(kv_dtype, str):
+        raise ValueError("InferCast memory budgets require explicit kv_cache_data_type")  # noqa: TRY004
+
+    capacity = hw.hbm_capacity_gb
+    try:
+        if (
+            isinstance(capacity, bool)
+            or not isinstance(capacity, (int, float))
+            or not math.isfinite(capacity)
+            or capacity <= 0
+        ):
+            raise ValueError
+        # Preserve the existing simulator's GiB convention, independent of host GPU.
+        capacity_bytes = int(capacity * (1 << 30))
+        if capacity_bytes <= 0:
+            raise ValueError
+    except (ValueError, OverflowError):
+        raise ValueError(
+            "target accelerator hbm_capacity_gb must be finite and positive"
+        ) from None
+
+    try:
+        import infercast
+
+        actual_revision = getattr(infercast, "__revision__", None)
+        if actual_revision != revision:
+            raise ValueError(
+                "memory_budget.provider_revision does not match installed InferCast "
+                f"(configured={revision!r}, installed={actual_revision!r})"
+            )
+        from infercast.sdk import (
+            MemoryBudgetPolicy,
+            ResourceTopology,
+            build_model_resources,
+            estimate_memory_budget,
+        )
+    except ImportError as error:
+        raise ValueError(
+            "InferCast with the resource-budget SDK is required"
+        ) from error
+
+    topology = ResourceTopology(
+        tp_size=target_config.tp_size,
+        ep_size=target_config.ep_size,
+        pp_size=target_config.pp_size,
+    )
+    policy = MemoryBudgetPolicy.from_dict(dict(budget_config["policy"]))
+    page_size = target_config.page_size or 1
+    config_path = Path(model.model_path).expanduser() / "config.json"
+    resources = build_model_resources(
+        model_id,
+        path=config_path,
+        topology=topology,
+        kv_cache_dtype=kv_dtype,
+        kv_page_size=page_size,
+        shared_expert_tp_size=budget_config.get("shared_expert_tp_size"),
+        revision=model_revision,
+    )
+    _validate_loaded_model(model, resources, config_path, target_config)
+    budget = estimate_memory_budget(
+        resources, device_capacity_bytes=capacity_bytes, policy=policy
+    )
+    max_tokens = budget.max_cache_tokens
+    if (
+        budget.status != "fits_declared_budget"
+        or type(max_tokens) is not int
+        or max_tokens <= 0
+    ):
+        raise ValueError(
+            "InferCast memory budget leaves no usable KV capacity "
+            f"(status={budget.status!r}, max_cache_tokens={max_tokens!r})"
+        )
+    metrics = {
+        "provider": "infercast",
+        "provider_revision": revision,
+        "model_id": model_id,
+        "resource_digest": resources.digest,
+        "provenance": resources.provenance.to_dict(),
+        "policy": policy.to_dict(),
+        "topology": topology.to_dict(),
+        "kv_cache_dtype": kv_dtype,
+        "kv_page_size": page_size,
+        "shared_expert_tp_size": budget_config.get("shared_expert_tp_size"),
+        "max_total_tokens": max_tokens,
+        "ranks": [
+            {key: value for key, value in rank.to_dict().items() if key != "tensors"}
+            for rank in budget.ranks
+        ],
+    }
+    return max_tokens, metrics

+"""A causal boundary around native scheduler results and external driver events."""
+
+import inspect
+import math
+import time
+from collections.abc import Callable
+from contextlib import contextmanager

+import zmq

+from sglang_simulator.compat import validate_coordinator_endpoint

+def install_prefill_cadence_hooks(target, coordinator_getter) -> None:
+    """Observe native cadence decisions without changing their counter or result."""
+    next_batch = getattr(target, "get_next_batch_to_run", None)
+    should_defer = getattr(target, "_should_defer_prefill", None)
+    if not callable(next_batch) or not callable(should_defer):
+        return  # A resolved positive interval is rejected by the runtime check.
+
+    @wraps(next_batch)
+    def wrapped_next_batch(self, *args, **kwargs):
+        bridge = coordinator_getter()
+        if bridge is None:
+            return next_batch(self, *args, **kwargs)
+        bridge._cadence_only_pass = False
+        bridge._cadence_deferred = None
+        bridge._in_scheduler_pass = True
+        try:
+            result = next_batch(self, *args, **kwargs)
+            bridge._cadence_only_pass = (
+                bridge._cadence_deferred
+                and getattr(result, "batch_to_run", result) is None
+            )
+            return result
+        finally:
+            bridge._in_scheduler_pass = False
+
+    @wraps(should_defer)
+    def wrapped_should_defer(self, *args, **kwargs):
+        bridge = coordinator_getter()
+        if bridge is None:
+            return should_defer(self, *args, **kwargs)
+        before = getattr(self, "_prefill_decode_interval_remaining", None)
+        result = should_defer(self, *args, **kwargs)
+        after = getattr(self, "_prefill_decode_interval_remaining", None)
+        if (
+            not bridge._in_scheduler_pass
+            or bridge._cadence_deferred is not None
+            or type(result) is not bool
+            or type(before) is not int
+            or type(after) is not int
+            or before < 0
+            or before > self.prefill_decode_interval
+            or after != (before - 1 if result else 0)
+            or (result and before == 0)
+            or (not result and before != 0)
+        ):
+            raise ProtocolError("unsupported native prefill cadence decision")
+        bridge._cadence_deferred = result
+        return result
+
+    wrapped_next_batch._simulator_cadence_hook = True
+    wrapped_should_defer._simulator_cadence_hook = True
+    target.get_next_batch_to_run = wrapped_next_batch
+    target._should_defer_prefill = wrapped_should_defer
+
+
+def _validate_prefill_cadence_runtime(scheduler) -> None:
+    interval = getattr(scheduler, "prefill_decode_interval", 0)
+    if type(interval) is not int or interval < 0:
+        raise ValueError("unsupported resolved prefill_decode_interval")
+    if interval == 0:
+        return
+    expected = {
+        "get_next_batch_to_run": ("running_batch", "last_batch"),
+        "_should_defer_prefill": (),
+        "_arm_prefill_decode_interval": ("batch",),
+    }
+    for name, parameters in expected.items():
+        method = getattr(scheduler, name, None)
+        if (
+            not callable(method)
+            or tuple(inspect.signature(method).parameters) != parameters
+        ):
+            raise ValueError(f"prefill_decode_interval requires native {name} surface")
+        if name != "_arm_prefill_decode_interval" and not getattr(
+            method, "_simulator_cadence_hook", False
+        ):
+            raise ValueError(f"prefill_decode_interval requires observed native {name}")
+    remaining = getattr(scheduler, "_prefill_decode_interval_remaining", None)
+    if type(remaining) is not int or not 0 <= remaining <= interval:
+        raise ValueError("prefill_decode_interval requires a valid native counter")
+
+
+def _watchdog_activation_owner(watchdog):
+    """Resolve the native raw callback without activating a disabled watchdog."""
+    missing = object()
+    active = getattr(watchdog, "is_active", missing)
+    if active is not missing:
+        owner = watchdog
+    else:
+        owner = getattr(watchdog, "_raw", missing)
+        if owner is missing:
+            from sglang.srt.utils.watchdog import _WatchdogNoop
+
+            if type(watchdog) is _WatchdogNoop:
+                return None
+            raise ValueError("unsupported native watchdog activation interface")
+        active = getattr(owner, "is_active", missing)
+    if not callable(active):
+        raise TypeError("native watchdog activation must be callable")
+    return owner, active

+class CoordinatedScheduler:
+    """Receive payloads while time is stopped; commit results at their due time.
+
+    One instance lives in the scheduler process. A server handles one coordinated
+    run, including its warmup; restarting it gives the next run a clean cache.
+    """
+
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        *,
+        scheduler,
+        endpoint: str,
+        timeout_s: float = 30.0,
+        pending_work: Callable[[], bool] | None = None,
+    ):
+        endpoint = validate_coordinator_endpoint(endpoint)
+        # Model defaults can resolve cadence absent from the raw launch arguments.
+        _validate_prefill_cadence_runtime(scheduler)
+        self.scheduler = scheduler
+        self._pending_work = pending_work
+        self.clock = Coordinator()
+        self.timeout_s = timeout_s
+        self._closed = False
+        self._token_events = None
+        self._watchdogs = []
+        self._context = zmq.Context()
+        self._socket = self._context.socket(zmq.REP)
+        try:
+            self._socket.setsockopt(zmq.LINGER, 0)

+The scheduler supplies the actual local batches. A cost adapter owns measured
+phase costs and a separate progress model owns native committed counts. Neither
+acceptance observations from the current call nor a speculative speedup are
+accepted as execution inputs. This module imports no SGLang or device runtime.
+"""

+CONTRACT = "sglang-dspark-step-v1"
+_DECODE_PHASES = (
+    "worker_preamble",
+    "proposal",
+    "target_verify",
+    "accept_commit_publication",
+    "worker_tail",
+)

+def _fail(message, **details):
+    raise PredictorError("invalid_dspark_step", message, **details)
+
+
+def _integer(value, minimum, label):
+    if type(value) is not int or value < minimum:
+        _fail(f"{label} must be an integer >= {minimum}")
+
+
+def _canonical_object(value, label):
+    if type(value) is not str:
+        _fail(f"{label} must be canonical JSON")
+    try:
+        parsed = json.loads(value)
+        canonical = json.dumps(
+            parsed, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":"), allow_nan=False
+        )
+    except (ValueError, TypeError) as error:
+        raise PredictorError("invalid_dspark_step", f"invalid {label}") from error
+    if not isinstance(parsed, dict) or not parsed or value != canonical:
+        _fail(f"{label} must be a nonempty canonical JSON object")
+    return parsed
+
+
+def _read_canonical_budget(value, label):
+    budget = _canonical_object(value, label).get("max_new_tokens")
+    return budget if type(budget) is int else None
+
+
+@lru_cache(maxsize=32)
+def _cached_canonical_budget(value, label):
+    # Retain only immutable validation metadata, never the parsed object.
+    return _read_canonical_budget(value, label)
+
+
+def _canonical_budget(value, label):
+    # The bound limits retention only; larger or non-builtin inputs retain the
+    # original validation/error path without hashing user-defined objects.
+    if type(value) is str and type(label) is str and len(value) <= 1024 * 1024:
+        return _cached_canonical_budget(value, label)
+    return _read_canonical_budget(value, label)

+class DSparkRequest:

+    extend_len: int

+    output_tokens_before: int

+            _fail("DSPark step must advance the run's forward sequence")
+        modes = {group.forward_mode for group in step.groups} - {"IDLE"}

+            )

+                        request.target_prefix_len,
+                        request.target_prefix_len,
+                        request.target_prefix_len,
+                    )
+                else:
+                    prior = CommittedHistory(
+                        request.target_prefix_len,
+                        known.draft_valid_from,
+                        min(known.draft_valid_to, request.target_prefix_len),
+                    )
+            else:
+                prior = self.history_for(request.rid)
+            if prior != expected:
+                _fail(
+                    "DSPark before-work differs from committed causal history",
+                    rid=request.rid,
+                )
+            if not prefill and request.draft_valid_to != request.target_prefix_len:
+                raise PredictorError(
+                    "data_unavailable",
+                    "DSPark commit cannot bridge an unknown draft KV gap",
+                    rid=request.rid,
+                )
+        # A missing cost must fail before generating progress or mutating history.
+        started = time.perf_counter()
+        timing = self.cost_model.predict_step(step)
+        if type(timing) is not DSparkStepTiming:
+            _fail("cost adapter must return typed complete DSPark timing")
+        timing.validate_for(step)

+            DSparkProgress(
+                step.forward_id,
+                tuple((r.rid, int(r.emits_output)) for r in step.requests),
+                "native_prefill_bonus_v1",
+            )
+            if prefill
+            else self.progress_model.predict_progress(step)
+        )
+        if type(progress) is not DSparkProgress:
+            _fail("progress model must return typed DSPark progress")
+        result = DSparkStepResult(
+            step,
+            timing,
+            progress,
+            local_attention_dp_rank,
+            time.perf_counter() - started,
+        )
+        return result
+
+    def commit(self, result: DSparkStepResult):
+        step = result.step
+        if step.forward_id <= self._last_forward_id:
+            _fail("DSPark result was already committed")
+        # Recheck before-state so an outstanding result cannot overwrite a
+        # different successful step. predict() does not advance any run state.
+        for group in step.groups:
+            for request in group.requests:

+                    request.draft_valid_from,
+                    request.draft_valid_to,

+                raise PredictorError(
+                    "data_unavailable",
+                    "DSPark commit cannot bridge an unknown draft KV gap",
+                    rid=request.rid,
+                )
+            new_prefix = request.target_prefix_len + (
+                request.extend_len if prefill else count
+            )
+            lower = (
+                request.draft_valid_from
+                if request.draft_valid_to == request.target_prefix_len
+                else request.target_prefix_len
+            )
+            updated[request.rid] = CommittedHistory(new_prefix, lower, new_prefix)
+        self._history = updated
+        self._last_forward_id = step.forward_id
+
+    def execute(self, step: DSparkStep, *, local_attention_dp_rank=0):
+        result = self.predict(step, local_attention_dp_rank=local_attention_dp_rank)
+        self.commit(result)
+        return result

+    def clear(self):
+        self._history.clear()

+"""Route native DSPark worker calls to an explicit model-free simulation adapter.
+
+There is deliberately no default cost or acceptance model. The adapter must
+implement actual prefill/injection, decode, allocation and result publication;
+until it is installed, a DSPark forward fails with an attributable data gap.
+"""
+
+from sglang_simulator.hook import BaseHook
+from sglang_simulator.simulation.sglang.dspark import (
+    DSparkStepResult,
+    dspark_result_from_native,
+)
+from sglang_simulator.time_predictor.base import PredictorError
+
+
+def _runtime():
+    from sglang_simulator.simulation.sglang.scheduler import C_SchedulerHook
+
+    predictor = C_SchedulerHook.INFERENCE_PREDICTOR
+    runtime = getattr(predictor, "dspark_runtime", None)
+    if runtime is None or not getattr(predictor, "supports_dspark", False):
+        raise PredictorError(
+            "data_unavailable",
+            "DSPark simulation requires complete worker costs and an independent progress model",
+        )
+    return runtime
+
+
+class C_DSparkDraftInputHook(BaseHook):
+    HOOK_CLASS_NAME = "DFlashDraftInputV2"
+    HOOK_MODULE_NAME = "sglang.srt.speculative.dflash_info_v2"
+    REQUIRED = False
+
+    @classmethod
+    def hook(cls, target):
+        original_prepare = target.prepare_for_decode
+
+        def prepare(self, batch):
+            from sglang_simulator.simulation.sglang.dspark_runtime import (
+                INPUT_ATTRIBUTE,
+                prepare_cpu_decode,
+            )
+
+            if getattr(self, INPUT_ATTRIBUTE, None) is not None:
+                return prepare_cpu_decode(self, batch)
+            return original_prepare(self, batch)
+
+        target.prepare_for_decode = prepare
+
+
+class C_DSparkWorkerHook(BaseHook):
+    HOOK_CLASS_NAME = "DSparkWorkerV2"
+    HOOK_MODULE_NAME = "sglang.srt.speculative.dspark_components.dspark_worker_v2"
+    REQUIRED = False
+
+    @classmethod
+    def hook(cls, target):
+        def initialize(
+            self, server_args, gpu_id, nccl_port, target_worker, draft_worker_cls=None
+        ):
+            # Reuse the native base lifecycle and target allocator. No model
+            # weights, fake draft runner or device acceptance kernel is created.
+            from sglang.srt.arg_groups.overrides import resolving_view
+            from sglang.srt.speculative.base_spec_worker import BaseSpecWorker
+
+            # Native resolution preserves raw CLI inputs, including an omitted
+            # target width. Read its declared Q6 through the owning view.
+            cfg = resolving_view(server_args)
+            BaseSpecWorker.__init__(self)
+            if getattr(cfg, "speculative_dspark_block_size", None) != 5 or (
+                getattr(cfg, "speculative_num_draft_tokens", None) != 6
+            ):
+                raise PredictorError(
+                    "unsupported_execution_profile",
+                    "DSPark simulator requires resolved draft Q5 / target Q6",
+                )
+            self.server_args = server_args
+            self.gpu_id = gpu_id
+            self.nccl_port = nccl_port
+            self._target_worker = target_worker
+            self._draft_worker = None
+            self._hosts_draft = True
+            self.model_runner = target_worker.model_runner
+            self.device = target_worker.device
+            self.gamma = 5
+            self.query_token_num = 5
+            self.verify_num_draft_tokens = 6
+            self.speculative_num_draft_tokens = 6
+            # These native base methods operate on the shared target pool when
+            # no physical draft model is present.
+            for name in (
+                "alloc_memory_pool",
+                "init_attention_backends",
+                "init_cuda_graphs",
+                "weight_update_runners",
+            ):
+                setattr(self, name, getattr(BaseSpecWorker, name).__get__(self, target))
+
+        def forward(
+            self, batch, on_publish=None, grammar_barrier=None, *, pp_proxy_tensors=None
+        ):
+            # Native Scheduler supplies this callback for every DSPark forward.
+            # The native worker only consumes it when batch.has_grammar; an
+            # explicitly grammar-free batch needs no callback or grammar model.
+            if (
+                grammar_barrier is not None
+                and getattr(batch, "has_grammar", None) is not False
+            ) or pp_proxy_tensors is not None:
+                raise PredictorError(
+                    "unsupported_execution_profile",
+                    "DSPark simulator has no grammar-overlap or pipeline adapter",
+                )
+            result = _runtime().forward_batch_generation(
+                worker=self, batch=batch, on_publish=on_publish
+            )
+            if type(dspark_result_from_native(result)) is not DSparkStepResult:
+                raise PredictorError(
+                    "invalid_dspark_step",
+                    "DSPark adapter omitted its causal step result",
+                )
+            return result
+
+        def finished(self, *, rid, natural_stop):
+            _runtime().note_request_finished(rid=rid, natural_stop=natural_stop)
+
+        def clear(self):
+            _runtime().clear_cache_pool()
+
+        def reject_budget_override(self, frac):
+            raise PredictorError(
+                "unsupported_execution_profile",
+                "DSPark simulator has no dynamic verify-budget adapter",
+            )
+
+        target.__init__ = initialize
+        target.forward_batch_generation = forward
+        target.note_request_finished = finished
+        target.clear_cache_pool = clear
+        target.set_dspark_forced_budget_frac = reject_budget_override
+        # The native observers depend on physical logits/acceptance buffers.
+        # Simulator/progress evidence is exposed by its predictor instead.
+        target.dump_info_records = lambda self: None
+        target.clear_info_records = lambda self: None
+        target.block_accept_estimate_log_suffix = lambda self: None
+        target.spec_v2_attn_backends = property(
+            lambda self: (self.target_worker.model_runner.attn_backend,)
+        )
